question: If for a data set, third quartile and median are equal, then Bowley’s coefficient of skewness is:
solution:
The correct answer is **(-1)**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Bowley's coefficient of skewness, also known as the quartile skewness coefficient, is a measure of skewness that compares the distance between the first quartile (Q1) and the median (Q2) with the distance between the median (Q₂) and the third quartile (Q₃) in a data set.
 
• The formula for Bowley's coefficient of skewness is: Sk = (Q₁ - 2Q₂ + Q₃) over (Q₃ - Q₁)
 
 
• When the third quartile (Q₃) and the median (Q₂) are equal, the numerator of the formula becomes 0, resulting in a coefficient of skewness of -1. This indicates a perfectly negatively skewed distribution, where the data is concentrated on the right side of the median.
 
• In such a case, the data distribution has a longer tail on the left side, indicating that the majority of the data values are smaller than the median.
 
 
 
• It's important to note that Bowley's coefficient of skewness is just one measure of skewness and other measures such as the Pearson skewness coefficient or the moment coefficient of skewness may yield different results.
